BiblicalUsage: The word names a shelter, a refuge, and it is one of the Bible's great promises. Isaiah says there shall be a tabernacle for a shadow in the daytime from the heat and a place of refuge from storm and rain, and God has been a strength to the poor and a refuge from the storm. Jeremiah calls God his hope in the day of evil, and the proverb says in the fear of the LORD is strong confidence, and His children shall have a place of refuge.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe a refuge is not a hiding hole but a strong place, and God is the shadow from the heat and the covert from the storm. I hold that the fear of the LORD is itself the refuge, because the child who fears God need fear nothing else.
